text:
maria: Quick sanity check — did an nsys capture of a TRT+vLLM run and the wrapper shows ~38% of GPU kernel time spent in trt_wrapper::sync_and_dispatch. Timeline has repeated small memcpy + kernel-launch-sync cycles during decoding. Anyone seen wrapper syncs that high?

maria: capture command I used: `nsys profile --output trt_vllm_syncs --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn,cublas --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx` then ran the decoder for ~60s with batch=8, seq=1024, quantized model.

kevin: can you paste the nsys top-down summary? which model and quant flags?

maria: model=llama2-13b-4bit, quant=nf4-int8 fallback, dynamic_batching disabled, kv_mode=default (warmup enabled). nsys summary snippet: 

```
# CUDA API Time (sampled)
Memcpy HtoD  : 41.2%  (lots of small transfers, 20-100KB)
Kernel Launch: 15.3%
Stream Sync  : 10.1%
Other        : 33.4%

# CUDA Kernel Time
trt_wrapper::sync_and_dispatch_kernel    : 39.1%
cublasLtMatmul                          : 24.7%
gelu_fp32                               : 12.3%
kv_cache_memcpy_kernel                  : 11.5%
other                                   : 12.4%
```

maria: perfetto timeline shows a repeating pattern per token: CPU enqueues -> small HtoD memcpy (kv slice) -> kernel launch -> host cudaEventSynchronize -> next token. So host-side syncs are interleaving with kernel execution.

tom: memcpy HtoD that high screams per-token KV copies. Are we pinning KV buffers? vLLM should reuse pinned pages for KV cache. If not pinned, every memcpy is falling back to pageable path which is slower and triggers syncs.

maria: We pinned the big KV buffer at startup, but the wrapper slices and does per-request host copies for dynamic-sized KV regions. The slice copy path does `cudaMemcpyAsync` then immediately `cudaEventSynchronize` to guarantee visibility for TRT enqueue. That's what the trace shows.

jess: I remember we added that immediate synchronize to avoid cross-stream hazards when TRT engines use their own stream per execution. That was a conservative fix. It avoids correctness issues but kills throughput. Could we use `cudaStreamWaitEvent` or stream callbacks instead of blocking `cudaEventSynchronize` on the host?

kevin: also check TRT engine config: do we have `TRT_USE_STREAM_PER_ENGINE=1`? Using one stream per engine + host sync ends up serializing. Running all engines on a shared stream often helps batch launches without host-side syncs (but depends on other constraints).

maria: current config: stream_per_engine=1, enable_cuda_graphs=0. I toggled `TRT_USE_STREAM_PER_ENGINE=0` in a quick run — reduced host syncs but we still see many tiny kernel launches and memcpy stalls. CUDA Graphs reduced launch overhead but correctness path still does host syncs in wrapper.

maria: quick perfetto snippet (aggregated events):

```
Event: token_cycle (avg)
  enqueue_cpu  : 0.6ms
  kv_memcpy    : 0.9ms (64KB chunks x N)
  trt_enqueue  : 0.4ms
  host_sync    : 1.2ms
  kernel_exec  : 2.8ms
  total        : ~6.0ms
```

tom: that host_sync 1.2ms is the killer. If we can change the wrapper to signal the engine stream with an event and not call `cudaEventSynchronize` from the host, we can overlap memcpy/launch for subsequent tokens.

jess: code pointer is in `eng-runtime/third_party/trt_wrapper/wrapper.cpp` around `dispatch_request`. It currently does:

```cpp
cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, sz, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, staging_stream);
cudaEventRecord(ev, staging_stream);
cudaEventSynchronize(ev); // <- blocks host/thread
engine->enqueue(..., engine_stream);
```

jess: replace with:

```cpp
cudaMemcpyAsync(..., staging_stream);
cudaEventRecord(ev, staging_stream);
cudaStreamWaitEvent(engine_stream, ev, 0);
// no cudaEventSynchronize
engine->enqueue(..., engine_stream);
```

kevin: +1 to that approach. Also double-check that TRT enqueue doesn't call `cudaStreamSynchronize` internally (some wrappers do for legacy reasons). We should run a build with `TRT_LOG_SEVERITY=info` and instrument `Profiler` callbacks to ensure engine doesn't internally sync.

maria: I prototyped the `streamWaitEvent` change locally. Early results: end-to-end GPU kernel time for wrapper dropped from ~38% to ~12% in the nsys kernel breakdown. Overall token p95 latency dropped by ~24%. Still seeing ~9% memcpy cost — likely due to lots of small HtoD transfers.

perf-bot: ci/perf queued: run/trt-vllm/sync-removal/1790123456 — status: queued.

kevin: nice. For the remaining memcpy, consider 2 strategies: (1) aggregate KV writes into fewer larger memcpy ops (coalesce per-batch) or (2) use pinned staging buffers and keep per-token slices on-device with a small ring buffer so we avoid HtoD each token. Option (2) needs a memory manager but could pay off.

maria: Agreed. Coalescing is easiest short-term: modify scheduler to coalesce per-token KV writes while waiting up to `min_batch_ms` (we currently use 5ms). Increasing `min_batch_ms` to 10-12ms lets us build bigger KV pages and amortize memcpy. But that trades latency for throughput.

jess: let's also add a microbenchmark: `tools/perf/kv_memcpy_microbench.py` that allocates pinned buffers and measures small-chunk vs coalesced copy throughput+latency. We should capture both host-visible latency and device memcpy throughput.

maria: Plan: 1) merge sync removal patch to wrapper (PR posted as `maria/avoid-host-sync-trt`), 2) run nsys perf sweep with coalescing off/on, 3) add KV microbench. I'll run the sweep and attach results.

kevin: I'll schedule a cluster run on Dedicated for tomorrow to validate tail lat under load. Also will try the CUDA Graphs path with the sync removal patch — graphs + no-host-sync might be the sweet spot.

maria: Thanks — updating the ticket: INF-723: TRT/vLLM wrapper syncs and KV memcopy hotpath. Assignments: maria (prototype + bench), kevin (cluster run + graphs), jess (scheduler heuristic changes / coalescing), tom (KV memory-manager design).

kevin: :thumbsup:

maria: If anyone wants the raw nsys `.qdrep`/perfetto traces, ping me and I'll drop them in the eng-runtime/artifacts channel.
